raw_response:
I would keep my land in the pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the better irrigated fields, and I would put a smaller piece into spring peanut. I would do that because wheat-maize rotation is still the steadiest way for me to hold yield and cash flow on the North China Plain, and I already know how to manage it well. I would not spread myself across too many crops, because that raises labor pressure and market risk for me. On the wheat land, I would push water and fertilizer carefully but not excessively, because water is never something I treat as unlimited. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize with no-tillage seeding where possible to save time and keep moisture. I would keep peanut only on a smaller area to spread risk a bit and make use of lighter soil, but I would not let it become my main crop because grain is still the backbone of my farm.
